skill.name: github-actions-templates
skill.description: Create GitHub Actions workflow templates for CI, Docker image builds, Kubernetes deployment, matrix testing, reusable workflows, security scanning, and production approvals.
skill.summary: Generate practical GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for common application delivery tasks.
skill.author: wshobson

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline file references, and GitHub Actions template syntax. The secret references use GitHub Actions secrets rather than local environment reads by the skill. One real hardening issue remains: two third-party actions use mutable master refs in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin aquasecurity/trivy-action and snyk/actions/node to trusted release tags or commit SHAs before publication.

remediation.issue: Long-lived AWS access key pattern in deployment example
remediation.suggestion: Prefer GitHub OIDC with an AWS role-to-assume, and document required minimal permissions for deployments.

remediation.issue: Production placeholders can be copied without review
remediation.suggestion: Label example domains, clusters, regions, namespaces, and notification targets as placeholders that must be replaced.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable GitHub Action References in Security Scan Template
semantic_findings.description: The security scan workflow uses third-party actions on mutable master refs: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master and snyk/actions/node@master. Mutable refs can change without review and create CI supply-chain risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced third-party actions are clearly pinned to master branches in the security scan example. This is a known workflow supply-chain risk, although it is not malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable CI/CD workflows without rebuilding common patterns from scratch. This skill provides GitHub Actions templates for tests, builds, deployments, scans, and approvals.
actual_capabilities: Provides Node.js test workflow patterns with npm caching and coverage upload.
Shows Docker image build and push workflows for GitHub Container Registry.
Includes Kubernetes deployment workflows using AWS credential setup and kubectl commands.
Provides matrix build examples for multiple operating systems and Python versions.
Shows reusable workflow, security scan, production approval, and Slack notification patterns.
limitations: Does not create repository-specific secrets, environments, or branch protection rules.
Requires users to adapt workflow names, paths, regions, clusters, and deployment commands.
Some examples use mutable action refs and should be pinned before production use.
Does not validate generated workflows against each repository configuration.

use_cases.title: Add Continuous Integration
use_cases.description: Create test workflows for pull requests and main branch pushes with dependency caching and coverage upload.

use_cases.title: Standardize Deployment Pipelines
use_cases.description: Draft workflows for Docker image publishing, Kubernetes deployment, and production approval environments.

use_cases.title: Introduce Security Scans
use_cases.description: Add vulnerability scan workflow patterns that publish results into GitHub security reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CI Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Node.js project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for a Node.js project. It should run on pull requests and main branch pushes, cache npm dependencies, run lint, run tests, and upload coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Add Docker Build Publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Publish container images after successful builds.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that builds a Docker image, tags it from branches and release tags, and publishes it to GitHub Container Registry with least-privilege permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Kubernetes Deployment Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Deploy an application after release approval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions workflow for deploying to an Amazon EKS cluster. Include environment approvals, minimal permissions, OIDC-based AWS authentication, kubectl rollout checks, and clear placeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Into Reusable Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing GitHub Actions workflows and convert repeated test, build, scan, and deploy steps into reusable workflows with documented inputs, secrets, permissions, and failure behavior.

output_examples.input: Create a Node.js test workflow for main and pull requests.
output: A workflow plan with push and pull request triggers.
A Node.js version matrix with dependency caching.
Separate install, lint, test, and coverage upload steps.

output_examples.input: Create a Docker publish workflow for GitHub Container Registry.
output: A workflow plan with registry login, metadata extraction, and image publishing.
Recommended package permissions for the GitHub token.
Caching guidance for faster Docker builds.

output_examples.input: Create a production deployment workflow with approval.
output: A deployment workflow outline with an environment approval gate.
Cloud authentication and kubeconfig setup steps.

best_practices: Pin third-party actions to trusted versions or commit SHAs before production use.
Use least-privilege GitHub token permissions for every workflow job.
Store deployment secrets in GitHub secrets or OIDC providers, never plaintext workflow files.
anti_patterns: Copying templates without replacing placeholder clusters, paths, and environments.
Granting broad write permissions when a job only needs read access.
Using mutable action branches for production workflows.

faq.question: Can this skill create workflows for Node.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Node.js test workflow patterns with dependency caching, linting, tests, and coverage upload.

faq.question: Does it support Docker image publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows workflows for building Docker images and publishing them to GitHub Container Registry.

faq.question: Can it help with Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides deployment workflow patterns with AWS credential setup, kubeconfig updates, and rollout checks.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets for me?
faq.answer: No. You must create repository secrets, environments, permissions, and cloud roles outside the generated workflow.

faq.question: Are the templates ready to copy into production?
faq.answer: They are starting templates. Review placeholders, pin action refs, set least-privilege permissions, and test in your repository.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflow generation tasks.
